cashmere.origin: Cashmere is the fine down grown by secondary follicles of cashmere-type domestic goats, referred to in US law as Capra hircus laniger. It is a fiber type produced by many breeds rather than a single breed. China and Mongolia supply most of the world's raw cashmere, and Mongolia's share has grown as Chinese output declined. Pashmina in the narrow sense is down from Changthangi goats of the high Changthang plateau of Ladakh. A goat typically yields a few hundred grams of raw down a year, less than half of which survives dehairing.
cashmere.structure: Cashmere down is keratin, with the same disulfide-stabilized filament and matrix chemistry as sheep wool, but the fibers are much finer. US law caps the mean diameter at 19 microns. The cuticle scales are thinner and lower at their edges than those of fine wool, a difference that scanning electron microscopy measures as scale height and that contributes to a smoother surface and softer hand. The coarse guard hairs of the same fleece are much thicker and stiffer, which is why their removal during dehairing matters so much for the quality of the finished yarn.
cashmere.process: Down is harvested during the spring molt, by hand combing in many herding systems or by shearing. Raw fiber is sorted by natural color (white, grey and brown lots are valued differently), then scoured to remove grease, dust and vegetable matter. Dehairing is the defining step: mechanical separation of fine down from coarse guard hair, a process industrialized in the late nineteenth century by Bradford firms such as Joseph Dawson Ltd of Cashmere Works. Dehaired fiber is dyed as loose stock or top and spun on woollen or worsted systems, and knitted fabric is often milled to develop bloom.
cashmere.performance: Cashmere shares wool's hygroscopic protein behavior, acid and metal-complex dye affinity, flame behavior and vulnerability to clothes moth and carpet beetle larvae. Because individual fibers are fine and relatively short, and yarns are often lightly twisted for loft, fabrics abrade and pill more readily than those of comparable weight in coarser wool, especially at friction points such as underarms and cuffs. The scaled surface can still felt under heat, moisture and agitation, so knitwear can shrink or thicken if washed aggressively.
cashmere.identify: Burn tests (indicative only, and to be done with care) cannot separate cashmere from wool, since both behave as keratin. Laboratories rely on light and scanning electron microscopy, measuring diameter and cuticle scale height at the scale edge; interlaboratory round trials organized for the CCMI have tested this approach on blends. Yak down looks very similar to cashmere under SEM and has been reported to cost about a quarter as much, making it a common adulterant alongside fine wool. DNA and targeted proteomic methods can detect such admixtures.
cashmere.labeling: In the US, 15 U.S.C. 68b (Wool Products Labeling Act, as amended) treats a product as misbranded if labeled cashmere unless the fiber is the fine dehaired undercoat of the cashmere goat with a mean diameter not over 19 microns, a coefficient of variation around the mean not over 24%, and no more than 3% by weight of fibers over 30 microns. In the EU, 'cashmere' is an Annex I name in Regulation 1007/2011 for hair of the kashmir goat. Voluntary programs include the Sustainable Fibre Alliance standards (Mongolia and China) and the Good Cashmere Standard of the Aid by Trade Foundation.
cashmere.past: Woven Kashmir shawls of fine goat down were luxury goods in Mughal and later courts, and their buta (boteh) motif was copied so extensively by nineteenth-century European mills, notably in Paisley, Scotland, that the design took the town's name. European industry then moved from importing shawls to importing raw down, and mechanical dehairing in Bradford made cashmere a knitwear fiber. After Mongolia's transition to a market economy, goat herds grew rapidly, and researchers and development agencies have linked that growth to rangeland degradation, prompting standards such as SFA's rangeland management requirements.
